summary.oneLiner:
Q4 FY26 was MobiKwik's second straight EBITDA- and PAT-positive quarter (full-year EBITDA near break-even
at -₹5cr vs -₹79cr in FY25; PAT loss halved to -₹62cr), driven by record payments GMV and a sharply
higher financial-services gross margin (59%, best-ever). Management is now deliberately re-investing the
~₹50cr/year of underlying core-business EBITDA into four growth engines — offline merchant payments,
online merchant acquiring (Zaakpay), an NBFC (co-lending upgrade from the current LSP model), and AI —
guiding to "baseline profitability" (i.e., stay bottom-line positive) through FY27-28 even as fixed costs
step up 15-20%.

one-line thesis: Q4 FY26 was MobiKwik's second straight EBITDA- and PAT-positive quarter (full-year EBITDA near break-even
at -₹5cr vs -₹79cr in FY25; PAT loss halved to -₹62cr), driven by record payments GMV and a sharply
higher financial-services gross margin (59%, best-ever). Management is now deliberately re-investing the
~₹50cr/year of underlying core-business EBITDA into four growth engines — offline merchant payments,
online merchant acquiring (Zaakpay), an NBFC (co-lending upgrade from the current LSP model), and AI —
guiding to "baseline profitability" (i.e., stay bottom-line positive) through FY27-28 even as fixed costs
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > One-offs: Q4 reported PAT includes a ₹3.76cr exceptional charge from Labour Wage Code changes (ex-that,
> underlying PAT ₹8.1cr); Q4 fixed costs include a ₹4cr one-off. FY26 EBITDA/PAT are also structurally
> depressed by ~₹55cr of discretionary merchant-payments investment that management says could have been
> avoided for a +₹50cr EBITDA print instead of the reported -₹5cr.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Payments + lending GMV growth: 30-35% in FY27 (both businesses).
EBITDA margin FY27: similar ~5% range to FY26 — i.e., core-business margin gains are guided to be
reinvested into growth engines rather than flow through to reported EBITDA.
Lending spread: management flags current 5.3-5.4% as elevated/not sustainable; long-term "sweet spot"
guided at 4-4.5% (previously guided range was 4-4.5%).
Payments take-rate: 12-15bps long-term (conservative vs current 16bps, due to regulatory uncertainty).
Fixed cost base: to grow 15-20% in FY27 (from ~₹115-120cr/quarter) as merchant-device rollout (higher
depreciation + distribution headcount) scales.
Merchant-payments investment: ~₹55cr in FY26 (opex, not capitalized except the device piece which sits
in depreciation); "similar range" of investment guided for FY27, continuing for at least 18 months.
Offline merchant payments: targeting 5x device scale-up to drive 10x revenue growth by FY28; EBITDA
breakeven targeted by FY28. Ambition: reach 10-20% of the market leader's scale within 18-24 months
across at least two of three focus categories (organized retail, oil & gas/petrol, mom-and-pop).
Online merchant acquiring (Zaakpay): targeting 10x GMV by FY28; EBITDA breakeven by FY28; focus
categories called out: education, government, BBPS.
NBFC roll-out timeline (from May 2026): (1) migrate existing LSP business to a new wholly-owned
subsidiary — 2-3 months; (2) NBFC entity setup — 3-6 months from today; (3) launch operations/disbursals
under co-lending — 6-9 months from today. Board/shareholder approval pending for capital infusion into
the NBFC subsidiary.
Merchant partner count: not being targeted as a KPI in isolation (grew only 7% in FY26 off a 4.9mn base)
— management explicitly de-emphasizes raw merchant count in favor of category-level share gains.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (services/platform business, no order book). Pipeline framed as: GMV growth precedes
revenue recognition — UPI-driven GMV (+170% YoY on customer-initiated UPI txns) and BBPS bill-pay GMV
(2.2x to ₹26,900cr in FY26, 48% 3-yr CAGR) are both described as revenue "in the pipeline" that will show
up through FY27 as PPI-over-UPI MDR (still not enacted by regulator) and UPI monetization mature.
segment / subsidiary detail: Consumer payments — wallet (India's largest by GTV, ~20% share), UPI (2nd-fastest-growing UPI app),
BBPS bill-payments (6th-largest COU by GTV; GMV ₹26,900cr FY26, 2.2x YoY, 48% 3-yr CAGR — company calls
this a "mature" business now scaling further).
Digital lending (LSP model today) — to be migrated into a new wholly-owned subsidiary ahead of NBFC
launch; digital-credit GMV ~₹3,200cr FY26; deliberately shifting mix toward super-prime (32% of
disbursals, up from 10%) and repeat borrowers (63.5%, up from 20%).
NBFC (new, regulatory approval received) — separate wholly-owned subsidiary; ring-fenced from
Holdco and from the LSP subsidiary by regulatory design; will be an additional lending partner
alongside existing LSP lender partners, not a replacement.
Zaakpay (online merchant acquiring, wholly-owned subsidiary) — targeting 10x GMV by FY28; first
quarter management has broken out sub-category disclosure (bill-pay, merchant payments, etc. within
payments) and plans to disclose more each quarter.
Offline merchant payments (PoS/soundbox devices) — 4.9mn merchant partners (+7% FY26); three focus
categories: organized retail, oil & gas/petrol, mom-and-pop; device rollout drives higher depreciation.
growth verticals / optionality: Four explicitly-named growth engines: (1) offline merchant payments, (2) online merchant acquiring
(Zaakpay), (3) NBFC/co-lending, (4) AI. AI stats cited: 80% of code AI-generated, 55% of early collections
AI-driven, 86% of customer support self-served by AI; management frames AI as a "compounding competitive
moat," not just a productivity tool (funnel-drop detection, personalization, cohort acquisition, real-time
fraud detection called out as forward use-cases — not yet quantified).
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona: Largest wallet in India by GTV (~20% share as of March 2026) — scale/network-effect claim, evidenced
by GMV data on the call.
Regulated lending stack: NBFC approval (received) plus 7 years of underwriting/collections/lender-
partnership experience management says will "seamlessly transition" from the LSP model — a licensing +
track-record moat vs newer digital-lending entrants, though NBFC not yet operational.
margins & cost dynamics: Contribution margin nearly doubled YoY (46% vs 23%) on payments/lending mix improvement. Financial-
services gross margin hit a record 59% on the super-prime/repeat-borrower shift. Offsetting this, fixed
costs rose to ₹117-120cr/quarter (+₹4cr QoQ, guided +15-20% in FY27) as device depreciation and
merchant-side headcount scale. Gross take-rate in payments has compressed due to UPI mix-shift (UPI GMV
growing fastest but PPI-over-UPI MDR still not enacted by the regulator) plus some lower-margin category
additions — management says net-level economics are still positive but flagged this explicitly as the
reason ex-UPI GTV growth (>30%) has not translated into revenue growth for several quarters.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No traditional capex; the analogous item is merchant-device rollout (soundboxes/PoS), capitalized into
depreciation (all other merchant-build costs — manpower, product — hit P&L directly, not capitalized).
₹55cr invested in FY26 in the merchant build-out (opex); similar quantum guided for FY27, for "at least
18 months." NBFC subsidiary capital infusion pending board/shareholder approval — watch for timing and
capital allocation: All long-term debt already repaid; only ₹261cr of short-term working-capital lines remain (used
specifically to bridge bank-holiday/weekend settlement gaps to merchants/customers). Net owned
unencumbered cash ₹434cr, but a meaningful chunk is still unutilized IPO proceeds not yet freely available
for deployment. Finance cost trending down (₹7.2cr Q3 → ₹5.1cr Q4). Capital for the new NBFC subsidiary
will require a fresh board/shareholder approval process to infuse funds (not yet done as of call date).
risks & watch-items: PPI-over-UPI MDR — regulator has not enacted the interoperability MDR management has been
expecting; this is the single largest explicit reason cited for consumer-payments revenue lagging GMV
growth. Timing remains regulator-dependent and unguided.
Payments take-rate regulatory risk — management explicitly refuses to model 16bps (current) for
2-3 years out, citing India's heavily regulated payments licensing regime; guides conservative 12-15bps.
Lending-spread reversion — 5.3-5.4% current spread flagged by management itself as elevated
(boosted by cohort-collection gains); long-term guide of 4-4.5% implies a margin step-down is expected.
Fixed-cost growth (15-20% FY27) outpacing near-term revenue growth in the new engines (merchant
breakeven not until FY28) — the "baseline profitability" promise is a thin (~1% PAT margin) cushion.
NBFC execution/timeline risk — multi-step regulatory sequencing (migrate LSP → set up NBFC →
launch disbursals), 12-18 months out from May 2026; capital infusion approval still pending.
Digital-credit GMV deceleration — sequential growth intentionally subdued this quarter; watch
whether this is purely a mix-quality choice (as management asserts) or an early demand/credit-quality
signal.
management quality / tone: Confident and consistent in messaging (Upasana Taku fielded most detailed questions; Bipin Preet Singh
handled strategic/competitive framing; Soham Roy handled cash/fixed-cost specifics). Management was candid
about the trade-off it is making (could report +₹50cr EBITDA today by not investing in merchant/NBFC
build-out) and explicit that near-term GMV-to-revenue lag in payments is a regulatory/mix issue, not
demand weakness. Slightly evasive on quantifying the eventual NBFC-vs-LSP lending mix ("too soon to say"
asked twice by the same analyst).
non-obvious takeaways: The "10x by FY28" merchant targets (both offline devices and Zaakpay GMV) are explicitly framed as a
deliberate choice over an earlier/smaller breakeven — management says they could break even 3-4x sooner
at lower scale but chose the larger scale-out because execution rigor + competitiveness are already in
place.
Management for the first time broke out payments sub-categories (bill-pay vs merchant payments etc.)
this quarter and plans to keep disclosing more — a signal that segment-level financial disclosure is
about to get materially richer (useful for future model granularity).
UPI transactions themselves generate no MDR for MobiKwik today; monetization on merchant payments comes
from credit-on-UPI-rails/RuPay credit card transactions, device rentals, and (eventually) merchant
credit — a clarifying disclosure on how the merchant-payments P&L will actually build out.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q4 FY26 (this): Back-to-back EBITDA+PAT positive quarters (Q3, Q4); record payments GMV (13th
straight quarter); financial-services gross margin hit record 59%; NBFC approval received but not yet
operational; four growth-engine reinvestment framing (merchant offline+online, NBFC, AI) introduced with
FY28 breakeven targets; fixed costs stepped up to ₹117-120cr and guided +15-20% for FY27.
Q1 FY27 → check: Did PPI-over-UPI MDR get enacted (biggest guided catalyst for payments revenue
reacceleration)? Progress on LSP→subsidiary migration (2-3 month guide from May 2026, due ~Jul-Aug 2026)
and NBFC entity setup. Did digital-credit GMV growth reaccelerate to the 30-35% FY27 guide? Did fixed
costs track the 15-20% guided increase, and did lending spread start compressing toward the 4-4.5%
"sweet spot"? Any quantification yet of NBFC-vs-LSP lending mix target.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
